latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Activity of the t(2;5) NPM-ALK or variant ALK fusion that drives constitutive STAT3, PI3K/AKT and ERK signaling in ALK-positive ALCL. Present (high) in ALK-positive systemic ALCL and absent in ALK-negative and most BIA-ALCL/PC-ALCL.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Uniform high-density CD30 (TNFRSF8) expression on neoplastic T-cells
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Universal strong CD30 staining of tumor cells defines ALCL. Required substrate for brentuximab-vedotin antibody-drug conjugate. Higher density correlates with stronger ADC effect.
Aggregate body burden of malignant CD30+ anaplastic T-cells in nodal and extranodal compartments. Drives nearly every clinical and laboratory abnormality of systemic ALCL.

IL-6, TNF-α and IFN-γ released by tumor cells and reactive macrophages drive fever, drenching night sweats, anorexia, weight loss, and acute-phase response. Especially prominent in ALK-negative and ALK+ small-cell variants.
Sinusoidal/parenchymal infiltration of liver and spleen by anaplastic lymphoma cells producing organomegaly, mild cholestatic LFT pattern, and contributing to cytopenias via splenic sequestration.
Marrow involvement by neoplastic CD30+ T-cells. Often patchy and detectable only by IHC; produces variable cytopenias and is more common in ALK-negative systemic ALCL and small-cell ALK+ variant.

Dermal and subcutaneous infiltration producing solitary or multifocal red-violaceous nodules with frequent ulceration. Defines primary cutaneous ALCL (indolent, often with spontaneous regression) and is a common extranodal site of systemic ALCL.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Extranodal visceral / soft-tissue / osseous ALCL infiltration
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Infiltration of lung, mediastinum, GI tract, soft tissue, and bone. Site-specific complications include lytic bone lesions, pulmonary nodules/infiltrates, GI obstruction or bleeding, and CNS involvement (rare).

CD30+ ALK-negative T-cell proliferation confined to fibrous capsule and seroma fluid around (typically textured) breast implants. Most cases are stage I with disease limited to capsule; minority show capsular invasion or distant spread.

Spontaneous or treatment-precipitated massive tumor cell turnover releasing K+, phosphate, urate and nucleic-acid breakdown products. Risk highest in bulky, high-LDH ALK+ disease and during the first chemotherapy cycle.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Lymphoma-associated macrophage activation / secondary HLH pressure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Tumor-driven IFN-γ and IL-6 produce hyperinflammatory macrophage activation; uncommon but disproportionately seen in ALK-negative ALCL and small-cell ALK+ variant. Manifests as hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, cytopenias and hepatic dysfunction.
PTHrP, 1,25(OH)2D and cytokine-mediated osteoclast activation by tumor cells produce hypercalcemia, particularly in ALK+ pediatric/young-adult systemic ALCL with bulky disease and bone involvement.

Functional T-cell dysfunction and reduced reactive T-cell repertoire due to tumor cytokines and tumor-mediated suppression. Increases risk of opportunistic infection (PJP, VZV, fungal) particularly when combined with chemotherapy and steroids.
Anthracycline + cyclophosphamide ± etoposide ± brentuximab marrow toxicity producing nadir neutropenia (day 7-14), anemia and thrombocytopenia. Drives febrile neutropenia hazard.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: ALK-positive subtype only
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: NPM-ALK constitutive kinase activity drives proliferation, survival and self-renewal of ALCL clones. Removal of ALK signaling (e.g. crizotinib) collapses tumor burden in ALK+ disease.
CD30 expression scales with the number of viable tumor cells. Burden reduction by chemo concurrently lowers CD30 antigen mass.
Nodal infiltration produces painless or tender lymphadenopathy, frequently bulky (>10 cm) in ALK+ pediatric disease.
Activated tumor T-cells shed sIL-2R; serum sCD25 correlates with burden and is elevated in essentially all systemic ALCL.
High cell turnover and tumor mass release LDH; serum LDH is an IPI component and tracks burden longitudinally.
LDH/ULN ratio is a normalized burden surrogate; values >2x ULN denote bulky/aggressive disease.
Tumor cytokine output scales with burden, especially in ALK-negative disease.
IL-6/TNF-α produce fever; classically intermittent and may exceed 38.5°C in ALK-negative ALCL.
Drenching night sweats are a classic B-symptom driven by cytokines.
Cytokine-mediated cachexia produces unintentional weight loss >10% in 6 months (B-symptom criterion).
Pro-inflammatory cytokines and anemia produce profound fatigue.
IL-6 is directly released by tumor and reactive cells.
Hepatic acute-phase response to IL-6 elevates CRP, often >50 mg/L.
Acute-phase fibrinogen elevation increases ESR; commonly markedly elevated.
Negative acute-phase reactant; hypoalbuminemia reflects sustained inflammation and is prognostic in ALCL.
Advanced systemic ALCL frequently spreads to liver and spleen via lymphatic and hematogenous routes.
Splenic infiltration produces moderate-to-massive splenomegaly.
Hepatic infiltration produces hepatomegaly and mild liver-test abnormalities.
Sinusoidal infiltration produces a cholestatic-pattern ALP elevation; bone involvement may also contribute.
Marrow involvement occurs in ~10-30% of systemic ALCL, more frequent in ALK-negative and small-cell variants.
Marrow replacement plus inflammatory iron sequestration cause normocytic anemia.
Marrow infiltration impairs megakaryopoiesis; splenic sequestration further lowers platelets.
Marrow replacement lowers neutrophil production.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Higher baseline in PC-ALCL subtype; common extranodal site in systemic ALCL
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Skin homing of CD30+ T-cells is a defining feature of PC-ALCL and a frequent secondary site in systemic disease.
Produces firm red-violaceous nodules, often ulcerating; may spontaneously regress in PC-ALCL.
Extranodal involvement (lung, bone, soft tissue, GI) is more common in ALCL than other PTCLs and is part of staging.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Risk highest with bulky disease, high LDH, high WBC, ALK+ pediatric disease and at chemotherapy initiation
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Bulk and high proliferative index translate into substantial cell-death load when chemotherapy is started.
Nucleic-acid breakdown raises uric acid; risks urate nephropathy.
Intracellular K+ release; arrhythmia risk.
Phosphate release precipitates Ca2+ producing hypocalcemia and tetany risk.
Urate and calcium-phosphate crystal nephropathy precipitate AKI.
Crystal nephropathy plus volume depletion is the leading TLS complication.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Disproportionate in ALK-negative systemic ALCL and small-cell ALK+ variant
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Tumor-derived IFN-γ/IL-6 amplify macrophage activation, occasionally precipitating frank lymphoma-associated HLH.
Hyperferritinemia (often >5000 ng/mL) marks macrophage activation.
TNF-mediated lipoprotein lipase suppression elevates triglycerides as part of HLH-2004 criteria.
Plasmin activation by tPA-rich macrophages consumes fibrinogen.
Threshold crossing produces lymphoma-associated HLH, a high-mortality complication of ALCL.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Particularly with bone involvement or pediatric ALK+ disease
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: PTHrP and calcitriol production by ALCL cells produces humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Opposes the TLS hypocalcemia direction; net calcium depends on which mechanism dominates
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pre-treatment hypercalcemia is sometimes the presenting feature in pediatric ALK+ ALCL.
Tumor cytokine milieu and clonal T-cell expansion suppress effective adaptive immunity.
Cellular immune dysfunction increases bacterial, fungal and opportunistic infection risk, compounded by chemotherapy.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Active during cytotoxic cycles only
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Anthracycline + cyclophosphamide (± etoposide, ± brentuximab) deplete neutrophil precursors.
Cytotoxic megakaryocyte injury produces thrombocytopenia at nadir.
Erythroid suppression and overlapping inflammation lower hemoglobin during therapy.
Neutropenia plus mucositis drives febrile neutropenia and bacteremia hazard, the dominant short-term iatrogenic risk.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only in advanced BIA-ALCL with axillary spread
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Axillary or supraclavicular adenopathy denotes higher-stage BIA-ALCL.
Untreated systemic ALCL is uniformly fatal; ALK-negative bulky high-IPI disease has the highest mortality.
Lymphoma-associated HLH carries high short-term mortality without rapid HLH-directed therapy plus lymphoma control.
TLS-associated AKI requiring dialysis worsens short-term outcome and limits chemotherapy intensity.
Treatment-related infections (febrile neutropenia, bacteremia, fungal pneumonia, PJP) are a leading non-relapse mortality cause.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: mediastinal_lymphadenopathy_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: deep_abdominal_lymphadenopathy_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: bulky_nodal_mass_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: metabolic_tumor_burden_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: extranodal_disease_extent_alcl captures extranodal or organ-specific lymphoma distribution relevant before biopsy confirmation.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: splenic_lesion_burden captures extranodal or organ-specific lymphoma distribution relevant before biopsy confirmation.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when the lymphoma has measurable nodal or splenic mass burden on imaging or examination.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Nodal lymphoma burden can be observed as a measured nodal mass diameter; preserve reported cm instead of guessing 0..1 severity.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when the lymphoma has measurable nodal or splenic mass burden on imaging or examination.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic involvement or splenic lymphoma burden can be followed as raw splenic size when reported.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Lymphoma tumor burden commonly first appears as pathologic nodal disease; satellites describe where and how large.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic lymphoma involvement is a parent imaging finding; size and burden are satellites/measurements.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Extranodal lymphoma involvement is a parent finding; organ-specific extent is a satellite.
Lymphoma cytokine activity produces recurrent or persistent fever over weeks to months.
Fever and inflammatory markers persist when the driver is lymphoma biology rather than ordinary bacterial infection.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most prominent with pulmonary IVLBCL, mediastinal bulky disease, pleural/pericardial involvement, or severe anemia.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pulmonary, mediastinal, extranodal, or microvascular lymphoma involvement can produce breathlessness.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More likely with airway/mediastinal compression or pulmonary infiltration.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pulmonary or mediastinal lymphoma involvement can produce cough.
Pure lymphoma fever does not produce bacterial bloodstream growth, although secondary infection can override this.
Systemic ALCL can produce IL-6/G-CSF-like inflammatory neutrophilia before chemotherapy.

axes.shape_free_text: Background near zero; rises with untreated tumor burden, HLH onset, severe TLS-AKI, refractory neutropenic sepsis. Falls with successful induction (especially BV-CHP in CD30+ disease) and consolidation.

Categorical: systemic ALK+ (best prognosis among systemic), systemic ALK-negative (intermediate), primary cutaneous ALCL (indolent), breast implant-associated ALCL (often surgery-curable). Static after diagnosis.
Binary IHC/FISH-defined ALK status. Stable over disease course. Defines crizotinib eligibility and modifies prognosis.
IHC-graded CD30 staining intensity and proportion (essentially 100% in ALCL). Required substrate for brentuximab vedotin.
0-5 IPI (age >60, stage III-IV, ECOG ≥2, LDH > ULN, >1 extranodal site). Recorded at diagnosis.
Lugano/Ann Arbor stage I-IV at diagnosis. Static absent progression.
Number of extranodal sites involved (skin, bone, lung, GI, liver, marrow, CNS).
Single mass ≥10 cm or mediastinal mass ratio >0.33. Modifies TLS risk and radiotherapy decisions.
Volume of effusion around textured breast implant; characteristic late-onset (median 8-10 years) BIA-ALCL presentation. Resolves after capsulectomy.
Histologic capsular wall invasion or mass beyond capsule, denoting higher-stage BIA-ALCL needing systemic therapy beyond capsulectomy.
Rises sharply at chemotherapy day 0-3 in bulky / high-LDH disease; near zero with effective rasburicase + hydration.
Rises during cytotoxic chemotherapy nadir (day 7-14 of each cycle); modulated by G-CSF and antimicrobial prophylaxis.
Painless or tender adenopathy, frequently bulky (>10 cm) particularly mediastinal in pediatric ALK+ disease. Falls rapidly with effective induction.
Moderate-to-massive in stage III-IV systemic disease.
Mild-to-moderate with hepatic infiltration.
Solitary or multifocal red-violaceous nodules ± ulceration. May spontaneously regress in PC-ALCL.
Intermittent fever common, especially in ALK-negative disease and small-cell ALK+ variant.
Drenching B-symptom; resolves rapidly with effective therapy.
Cachectic loss; >10% body weight in 6 months satisfies B-symptom criterion.
Driven by anemia plus cytokine load.
Elevated in majority of systemic ALCL; correlates with burden; IPI component.
Normalized LDH burden surrogate; ratio ≥2 denotes high-risk disease.
Elevated in essentially all systemic ALCL; component of HLH criteria when very high.
Variable: leukocytosis with reactive shift, or leukopenia with marrow involvement / chemotherapy nadir.
Untreated systemic ALCL can show cytokine-driven neutrophilia or leukemoid inflammation; marrow infiltration or chemotherapy can later drive neutropenia.
Often low at presentation (lymphopenia, IPI-equivalent prognosticator); may rise with circulating lymphoma cells in leukemic small-cell variant.
Normocytic anemia common; nadir during chemotherapy.
Thrombocytopenia from marrow infiltration and chemotherapy; very low values raise HLH suspicion.
Hypoalbuminemia is a prognostic marker in PTCL/ALCL.
Net hypercalcemia from PTHrP/calcitriol may dominate at presentation; hypocalcemia may emerge with TLS at chemotherapy initiation.
Elevated with high burden; surges with TLS unless rasburicase used.
Hyperkalemia in TLS phase.
Rises with TLS-AKI, urate or calcium-phosphate nephropathy.
Mild-to-moderate elevation with hepatic infiltration or bony involvement.
Mild rise with hepatic infiltration; can rise sharply with hepatitis B reactivation under therapy.
Markedly elevated when macrophage activation/HLH supervenes (often >5000 ng/mL).
Elevated in HLH-spectrum complications.
Falls in HLH; elevated as acute-phase reactant in active disease without HLH.
Elevated, drives B-symptoms and acute-phase response.
Elevated; correlates with cytokine load and B-symptoms.
Often markedly elevated.
Rises with disease burden, chemotherapy, steroids and post-transplant immunosuppression.
Drives febrile neutropenia, bacteremia, opportunistic (PJP, fungal, VZV) infection.
Low at baseline; rises in ALK-negative disease, small-cell ALK+ variant, refractory disease, and at relapse.
Spikes with TLS at induction; sustained rise with hypercalcemia or sepsis.
Rises with cumulative anthracycline exposure; modulated by baseline LV function.
Imaging-visible mediastinal lymph node enlargement or nodal packets, not the CT test itself.
Imaging-visible retroperitoneal, mesenteric, porta hepatis, para-aortic, pelvic, or other deep abdominal nodal disease.
Large confluent nodal mass or bulky nodal conglomerate by exam or imaging.
Whole-body active lymphoma burden inferred from PET avidity, multi-station mass burden, or equivalent staging imaging.
Focal or multinodular splenic lymphoma lesion burden distinct from palpable splenomegaly alone.
Extent of ALCL outside conventional nodal stations, including skin, breast-implant capsule, viscera, bone, lung, liver, spleen, or other extranodal sites.
Largest reported nodal or nodal-conglomerate diameter on CT/MRI/ultrasound or physical measurement; raw size, not a guessed severity score.
Largest splenic long-axis dimension on imaging; raw measurement when available.
Pathologic lymph node enlargement or nodal mass is present by examination or imaging. Parent finding for nodal distribution and size satellites.
Focal or multinodular splenic lesion suspicious for lymphoma is present. Parent finding for splenic lesion burden and splenic size satellites.
Extranodal mass, organ lesion, or tissue infiltration suspicious for lymphoma is present. Parent finding for organ-specific extranodal extent satellites.
History-level fever burden over days to months, distinct from a single measured body temperature.

axes.display_name: Lack of clinical response to standard antibacterial therapy
axes.shape_free_text: Persistent fever, inflammation, or organ findings despite antibacterial therapy that should have covered ordinary bacterial infection.
Patient-reported or observed breathlessness from pulmonary, cardiac, mediastinal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement.
Dry or productive cough as a symptom axis; mechanism depends on pulmonary, airway, cardiac, or mediastinal involvement.
Probability that standard blood cultures grow a causative bacterium; expected to remain low in uncomplicated lymphoma fever.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Same measurement up to a normalization constant.
Higher IPI is independently associated with worse PFS/OS in PTCL/ALCL.

axis_couplings.conditionality: PC-ALCL and stage I BIA-ALCL ≪ ALK+ systemic < ALK- systemic
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Subtype is the dominant prognostic stratifier independent of IPI.
ALK+ disease has substantially better 5-year OS than ALK- (≈70-90% vs 30-50%).
Bulky high-LDH disease is a TLS-risk-defining feature.
Hazard rises sharply once ANC drops below 0.5 x10^9/L.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Only the BIA-ALCL category drives this axis
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Periprosthetic seroma is essentially exclusive to BIA-ALCL among ALCL subtypes.
PC-ALCL is defined by isolated cutaneous involvement without systemic disease at diagnosis.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Large active lymphoma burden can raise turnover and inflammatory burden, but effect varies by subtype and bulk.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anatomic/metabolic lymphoma burden is a driver of LDH and inflammatory marker elevation rather than a laboratory test name.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Large active lymphoma burden can raise turnover and inflammatory burden, but effect varies by subtype and bulk.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anatomic/metabolic lymphoma burden is a driver of LDH and inflammatory marker elevation rather than a laboratory test name.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Brentuximab vedotin requires CD30 expression for ADC delivery; ALCL is universally CD30+ so this is met by definition.
ECHELON-2 demonstrated superior PFS/OS over CHOP for systemic CD30+ PTCL with ALCL driving the benefit.
Higher IPI reduces but does not abolish BV-CHP benefit.
ALK+ tumors derive especially deep responses; ALK- patients still benefit relative to CHOP.

side_effects.interpretation: Includes PJP, VZV, bacterial; warrants prophylaxis

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard induction for newly diagnosed systemic CD30+ ALCL (both ALK+ and ALK-).

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: ALK+ disease responds well to anthracycline-based therapy with 5-year survival often >70%.
High IPI markedly reduces CHOP cure fraction in ALK-negative disease.

treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative anthracycline-based induction when BV-CHP is unavailable, contraindicated, or as historical regimen.

side_effects.interpretation: Generally less marrow toxicity than combination chemo

treatments.context_specific_role: Relapsed/refractory systemic ALCL, multifocal PC-ALCL, and as bridging therapy to transplant.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Crizotinib targets ALK kinase activity; useless in ALK-negative disease.

treatments.context_specific_role: Relapsed/refractory ALK-positive ALCL, often as bridge to allogeneic transplant; pediatric and selected adult use.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Consolidative auto-SCT is most often offered in ALK-negative high-risk first complete remission.

treatments.context_specific_role: Consolidation in chemo-sensitive ALK-negative systemic ALCL in first remission, or chemo-sensitive relapsed disease.
Selected refractory or post-auto-SCT relapsed systemic ALCL; primarily young, fit patients.
Solitary PC-ALCL, residual masses post-chemotherapy, palliation of bulky symptomatic disease, and selected stage I BIA-ALCL with positive margins.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Stage IA BIA-ALCL confined to capsule has >90% durable cure with complete capsulectomy alone.
Capsular invasion or mass requires adjuvant systemic therapy and/or radiation.

treatments.context_specific_role: Definitive therapy for BIA-ALCL stage I; also performed in higher-stage BIA-ALCL combined with systemic therapy.

side_effects.interpretation: Predisposes to PJP and bacterial infection

treatments.context_specific_role: Pre-phase debulking, B-symptom and hypercalcemia control, component of CHP/CHOP, never as monotherapy outside the prephase setting.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hydrogen-peroxide byproduct triggers severe hemolysis and methemoglobinemia in G6PD deficiency.
Greatest benefit in high-risk TLS scenarios.

treatments.context_specific_role: Prophylaxis or treatment of TLS in high-risk ALCL initiating cytotoxic therapy.

side_effects.interpretation: Including rare DRESS/SJS in high-risk patients

treatments.context_specific_role: Primary or secondary prophylaxis after BV-CHP/CHOEP nadir; mobilization for autologous transplant.
PJP prophylaxis throughout chemoimmunotherapy and steroid courses, particularly when prolonged steroids or transplant-associated immunosuppression are used.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Indicated when HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ undergoing immunosuppressive therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Prevent HBV reactivation during chemoimmunotherapy; required in HBsAg+ and considered for anti-HBc+ patients.

alk_positive.trajectory_modulation: Younger age (often pediatric/young adult), bulky disease and B-symptoms common; lower mortality_hazard_in_D-ALCL with treatment.

alk_negative.trajectory_modulation: Older patients, more frequent B-symptoms, higher relapse rate, higher mortality_hazard_in_D-ALCL even with BV-CHP.

systemic_alk_positive.trajectory_modulation: Best prognosis among systemic ALCL; often pediatric/young adult; standard induction is BV-CHP or CHOP-based.

systemic_alk_negative.trajectory_modulation: Higher mortality, higher relapse rate; consolidation auto-SCT often considered in CR1.

primary_cutaneous_alcl.trajectory_modulation: Indolent skin-limited course; observation, surgery or local radiation often sufficient; spontaneous regression possible.

breast_implant_associated_alcl.trajectory_modulation: Late-onset (median 8-10 yr post-implant); stage I capsule-confined disease often cured by complete capsulectomy with implant removal.

young_under_40.trajectory_modulation: Higher proportion of ALK+ disease; better tolerance of intensive chemotherapy and transplant.

older_over_60.trajectory_modulation: Higher proportion ALK-negative; reduced chemotherapy tolerance; higher infection and cardiotoxicity risk.

macrotextured_implant_present.trajectory_modulation: Strong association with BIA-ALCL specifically; risk concentrated in macrotextured surfaces. Routine prophylactic explant of asymptomatic patients not indicated.

smooth_implant_or_no_implant.trajectory_modulation: Baseline risk; BIA-ALCL very rarely reported in smooth-only patients.

present.trajectory_modulation: Increases all NHL incidence including ALCL; complicates chemotherapy with infection and cytopenias; alters drug-drug interactions (especially with antiretrovirals).

high_3_to_5.trajectory_modulation: 5-year OS 30-50%; favors intensified induction and consolidation strategies.

stage_I_II.trajectory_modulation: Lower extranodal burden, lower TLS risk, higher cure rate.

stage_III_IV.trajectory_modulation: Greater B-symptom and HLH risk, higher TLS and AKI risk at induction.

deficient.trajectory_modulation: Contraindicates rasburicase due to oxidative hemolysis; modifies TLS prophylaxis algorithm to allopurinol-based.

HBsAg_positive_or_anti_HBc_positive.trajectory_modulation: Marked HBV reactivation risk during chemoimmunotherapy, especially with steroids and any B-cell depleting agents; mandates entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis.

reduced_LVEF_below_50_percent.trajectory_modulation: Limits or contraindicates anthracycline; supports anthracycline-sparing approaches such as gemcitabine-based or brentuximab-substituted regimens with cardiology co-management.

supportive_care: Tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis: aggressive isotonic IV hydration to maintain urine output >2 mL/kg/hr, allopurinol for low/intermediate risk, rasburicase for high risk (bulky disease, LDH >2x ULN, marked leukocytosis); avoid potassium and phosphate supplementation at induction
G6PD screening prior to first rasburicase dose; substitute allopurinol if deficient
Frequent (q4-q12h) chemistry monitoring during the first 24-72 hours of cycle 1 with attention to potassium, phosphate, calcium, urate, and creatinine
Prevention of febrile neutropenia: primary or secondary G-CSF after BV-CHP or CHOEP
PJP prophylaxis with TMP-SMX during chemoimmunotherapy and prolonged steroid courses, with atovaquone or dapsone (after G6PD screen) as alternatives
VZV prophylaxis with acyclovir/valacyclovir during and after intensive therapy or transplant
Antifungal prophylaxis (fluconazole or mold-active agent) in prolonged neutropenia and in transplant recipients
HBV screening (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before therapy with entecavir or tenofovir prophylaxis when indicated; HCV and HIV screening
Baseline echocardiogram or MUGA for left ventricular function before anthracycline; periodic monitoring during therapy and in long-term follow-up
Peripheral neuropathy assessment at every cycle of brentuximab-containing therapy; dose reduction or discontinuation of brentuximab and vincristine for grade ≥2 neuropathy
Fertility counseling and gamete preservation prior to alkylator-containing chemotherapy or transplant in patients of reproductive age
Anti-emetic prophylaxis using NK1 antagonist + 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone for highly emetogenic regimens
Mucositis and oral care regimen, especially during neutropenic nadir and post-transplant
VTE risk assessment given malignancy- and steroid-associated hypercoagulability; thromboprophylaxis during hospitalization

Vaccination review (inactivated influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19, recombinant zoster) timed away from chemotherapy nadir; live vaccines avoided during and after immunosuppression per transplant guidelines
Nutritional and physical-therapy support for cachexia and deconditioning
Psychosocial support and adolescent/young-adult oncology resources where applicable, given that systemic ALK+ ALCL frequently affects this age group
Surveillance imaging and labs after end-of-treatment per response-adapted schedule with attention to relapse patterns (especially CNS, skin, and bone marrow in ALK+ disease)

For BIA-ALCL: complete capsulectomy with implant removal as definitive surgery for stage I disease, multidisciplinary plastic surgery and lymphoma team evaluation, contralateral implant assessment, and longitudinal seroma surveillance

Long-term survivorship: monitoring for cardiomyopathy, secondary malignancy (especially after auto-SCT and alkylator exposure), endocrine dysfunction post-transplant, and chronic GVHD if allo-SCT performed
